title: Common
description: Shared definitions for all GlassWorld contracts (v0).

ContractVersion.description: Contract version. Incompatible changes require a new major version and an ADR.

RequestId.description: Unique id of a request, set by the core. Lowercase UUID.

Tick.description: Simulation tick the message refers to.

VocabId.description: Language-neutral vocabulary id (English snake_case, dot-separated namespaces).

EntityId.description: Id of an object or inhabitant instance in the world, assigned by the core.

OptionId.description: Id of an offered option, unique within one request.

LevelEntry.description: A named level 0..1 (need satisfaction, emotion intensity or trait strength).

KnownProperty.description: What the inhabitant believes about an object property (belief, not world truth).

source.description: model = real LLM, mock = test double, replay = answer replayed from a log.

attempts.description: Model calls used (1 + at most 2 retries, per handbook).

KnowledgeSource.description: How the inhabitant came to know it (concept): experienced = tried it, sure; heard = as sure as the trust in the teller; guessed = a guess (AI, or from what one has seen); read = as sure as the source seems; seen = looked at it closely, only what can be seen (TL #19921, added in 0.2 without breaking older readers).

Subject.description: What a knowledge entry or question is about: a type of thing, one object, a person or an event kind.

KnowledgeEntry.description: One belief of an inhabitant with its origin (B4a R3). The world keeps the truth; this is what the inhabitant believes.

told_by.description: Teller for source heard (or writer for read); null otherwise.

place.description: Where it was (B2533), null if not tied to a place. Optional: absent = unknown (older cores).

object.description: The object instance it was about (B2533), null if none. Optional: absent = unknown.

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls the kind of thing the belief is about (subject of kind type), by its own knowledge only: the inhabitants' name of an invention it believes anything about (it invented it, built it, tried it, looked at it, was told about it). Absent when it knows nothing of it, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key, i18n key vocab.object.<id>). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built. Optional (absent also from an older core).

MemoryEvent.description: One remembered event, language-neutral (kind + ids); the core picks the important ones.

place.description: Where it was (B2533), null if not tied to a place. Optional: absent = unknown (older cores).

object.description: The object instance it was about (B2533), null if none. Optional: absent = unknown.

times.description: How often it happened: an everyday event that repeats about the same subject is counted on one entry instead of listed again (data in the core); tick is then the last time. Optional: absent = 1.

outcome.description: What came of it, for a remembered action (absent for other events): done, found_out or nothing. An attempt is not a deed: 'drink' about flint with found_out or nothing means it tried and nothing happened.

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls the subject (about), by its own knowledge only: the own name of another inhabitant once it has learned it, the inhabitants' name of an invention it knows. Absent when it knows none, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built, so a name learned later shows in earlier events.

MemoryOutcome.description: What the core knows came of a finished action, by the one measure its repetition guard uses (W1696): done = the action had its effect (a need, a mood or the will to live changed, or the thing was used up); found_out = it changed nothing itself, but something was learned through it (e.g. that the thing is not drinkable); nothing = neither, it was without any effect.

Memory.description: Short life summary (English, condensed by the AI service, B4a R5) plus the latest important events.

summary.description: Internal English text for the AI (B4a R5); never shown to the player (player texts only via keys or GeneratedText).

Relationship.description: How this inhabitant feels about another one (B4a R7, values 0..1).

Habit.description: A routine or preference that grew from repetition (B4a R6).

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls the kind of thing the habit is about (about of kind type), by its own knowledge only: the inhabitants' name of an invention it believes anything about (it invented it, built it, tried it, looked at it, was told about it). Absent when it knows nothing of it, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key, i18n key vocab.object.<id>). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built. Optional (absent also from an older core).

needs.description: Need satisfaction: 0 = fully unsatisfied (urgent, e.g. hunger 0.1 = very hungry), 1 = fully satisfied. Sorted by id by the core.

mood.description: Current emotions with intensity 0 = absent, 1 = very strong. Only emotions above zero are listed. Sorted by id by the core.

traits.description: Long-term character traits, 0 = very low, 1 = very high. Sorted by id by the core.

will_to_live.description: Main wellbeing value, normalised to 0..1 (shown to the player as 0-100).

knowledge.description: Relevant beliefs (about perceived things first), sorted by subject.

relationships.description: Towards perceived inhabitants, sorted by id.

worn.description: What the inhabitant wears (B2540), one part per slot at most. Optional until the core sends it (absent = unknown).

felt_temperature_c.description: Temperature as the inhabitant feels it (weather, height, clothing; computed by the core, B2540), or null without weather. Optional until the core sends it.

conditions.description: What the inhabitant feels (B2543), at most one entry per condition and body part (the core guarantees it). Optional until the core sends it (absent = nothing known).

life_stage.description: B9 R1: life phase from age (vocabulary life_stage, data). Optional: absent = unknown (older cores).

age_years.description: B9 R1: age in life years (content/life/aging.json days_per_life_year). Optional.

family.description: B9 R4: kinship as this inhabitant knows it; the values (affection, trust) stay in relationships. 'other' may have died and no longer be perceivable (deceased). Optional.

reputation.description: B9 R6: own reputation in the settlement, 0..1. Optional.

settlement.description: B9 R21: the settlement and its style context (sayings, DE/EN). Optional.

culture.description: B9 R18/R19: culture entries relevant now (rituals, festivals, rules, sayings, beliefs); beliefs carry low certainty. Optional.

grief.description: B9 R17: mourning, at most three overlapping losses. Optional.

name.description: B9 R11 / Marcel W1698: the inhabitant's own name, so it can introduce itself; absent while it has none. Optional.

InhabitantState.description: Everything the AI may know about the inhabitant it speaks for (shared by decider and questions).

Thought.description: AI-generated thought bubble in the player's language (one short sentence).

GeneratedText.description: Player-facing text generated at runtime (not a translation key, ADR-0007 exception for AI texts).

text.description: Text in the player's language, generated by the AI and checked by the content guard.

JobKind.description: What a generation job produces (B7 R1). Payload and result carry the part of the same name; a kind without a payload definition is not supported yet.

JobState.description: queued = waiting; running; done = result ready; failed = error set; deferred = moved to the next computing night (B7 R4).

ServiceErrorCode.description: HTTP mapping: timeout=504, model_unavailable=503, overloaded=503, invalid_model_output=502, bad_request=422, forbidden=403 (host or session token), not_found=404, internal=500.

Invention.description: An idea for a thing that does not exist yet in the world (B4b). A record, never code: what it is for, from which perceived materials, how big, in which steps, and which true properties the new thing brings (only vocabulary ids). Inventions are things or buildings, never living beings (B2531).

name.description: Name in German and English (generated, checked by the content guard); the chronicle uses it as a parameter.

purpose.description: Action the thing is made for (vocabulary action).

materials.description: Object types the inhabitant perceives and wants to use (must be perceived; the core checks).

introduces.description: True properties of the new thing (property vocabulary only).

tech_level.description: Tech level the invention needs (vocabulary tech_level).

InventionStep.description: One building step: what is done with which materials.

process.description: Basic process (vocabulary process), e.g. split, bind, shape.

materials.description: Materials of this step (subset of Invention.materials).

PropertyCondition.description: Matches an object by its TRUE properties, never by type id (B1-2): all of properties_all and none of properties_none.

ProcessRule.description: A processing rule (B2537): a basic process applied to inputs matched by properties, with tool, heat and tech level, and what comes out. Same form in content/processes/rules.json and in AI-found world rules (job process), so both are applied the same way.

id.description: Stable rule id. Data rules: chosen in the data. World rules found by the AI: 'world_' + the first 16 hex digits of the process signature hash (see ProcessSignature), set by the service from the payload and checked by the core, never taken from the model.

tool.description: What the tool must be like, or null.

heat_min.description: Lowest heat level needed (vocabulary heat_level), or null.

ProcessOutcome.description: What the process does: change the properties of the (first) input, or produce an object type (catalog or invention).

produces.description: Object type that comes out, or null when the input only changes.

consumes.description: Indices (0-based) of the inputs that are used up; the first input changes (add/remove) unless it is consumed and produces is set.

ObservedThing.description: A thing as the inhabitant sees it: type and observable properties only (no hidden truth).

label.description: What THIS inhabitant calls this kind of thing (type), by its own knowledge only: the inhabitants' name of an invention it believes anything about (it invented it, built it, tried it, looked at it, was told about it). Absent when it knows nothing of it, and for things the data name (the id is the vocabulary key, i18n key vocab.object.<id>). Never a truth the inhabitant does not know; resolved when the message is built. Optional (absent also from an older core).

SoundKind.description: one_shot = a single short sound, loop = repeats while the thing runs (B2530). Shared by the rule guard's SoundDecision and the base sound library (GW3).

ProcessSignature.description: What makes two tries 'the same' (B2537): process, the TRUE property sets of the inputs and the tool, and the heat level. Canonical JSON: every property list deduplicated and sorted ordinally by code point; inputs sorted by their property list joined with ',' (ordinal comparison); 'no tool' is null, never an empty list; keys sorted; no spaces; UTF-8. Hash = sha256 of it, world rule id = 'world_' + first 16 hex digits. Test vectors: contracts/testvectors/process-signature.json. Note: the signature carries TRUE properties; the judge (world role) may see the truth, but it never goes into inhabitant texts (thought).

NewNeed.description: A need the invention brings (B4b R11, D333 format). Display names DE/EN come with the record because the vocabulary grows at runtime.

NewAbility.description: An ability the invention brings (B4b R11, D333 format).

LocalizedName.description: A generated name in both game languages (B4b R24, TL P9=A): the player can switch the language at any time.

WornItem.description: One worn part (B2540): its slot, its type and what the inhabitant BELIEVES about it (beliefs, not the truth).

slot.description: Slot (vocabulary slot, e.g. body, legs, feet, head, over).

properties.description: Properties the inhabitant believes the part has (e.g. warming, water_repellent).

FeltCondition.description: How the inhabitant feels (B2542/B2543): a felt state or symptom (vocabulary condition, e.g. feverish, weak, pain, nauseous), never the cause (the world knows the truth, the AI guesses). The core maps its internal cause to felt conditions through data.

severity.description: 0 = barely, 1 = as strong as it gets.

body_part.description: Where it is felt (vocabulary body_part), or null.

Place.description: Where something was met (B2533): horizontal world position in metres; the core keeps the full truth.

other.description: The relative; may no longer be perceivable when deceased.

relation.description: Vocabulary kinship: partner, parent, child, sibling (data).

SettlementContext.description: Settlement style context for idioms (B9 R21).

CultureEntry.description: A culture entry the inhabitant knows (B9 R18/R19); text is generated and checked by the guard.

kind.description: ritual, festival, rule, saying or belief (vocabulary culture_kind).

ProperName.description: A readable proper name invented by the AI (B9 R11): one word in Latin letters, the same in DE and EN, no translated text; the core and the guard check length, readability and youth protection.
